prose_updates.tldr: The paper gives a sound-and-complete finite compatibility criterion for exact-support linear non-Gaussian feedback graphs with latent variables and joint perfect-intervention response kernels. A moment-free intervention pushforward, a Bernoulli source-partition diagnostic, exact affine and Hall--Rado realization, and simultaneous translation-response constraints reduce equality to coupled finite charts for one common mechanism and source tuple. A second theorem proves that the zero-allowed class is exactly the finite union of exact-support strata and gives its corresponding downward-closed cover and compiler. The square no-latent reduction uses translations rather than means; the covariance witness and bounded-Laplace confidence rung retain moments only in their stated submodels.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. Graphical intervention equivalence for latent acyclic models and second-order recovery under rich experiments address different objects.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a finite coupled invariant that simultaneously represents exact structural completion, zero-allowed support strata, invisible or merged independent sources, principal intervention translations, and common-mechanism gluing on every lower-dimensional stratum, without population moment assumptions.
project_justification.fill: The exact-support theorem reduces mechanisms to affine, rank, Hall--Rado, and principal-minor charts; an unrestricted Bernoulli factorization reduces source-law containment to finite proportional-column surjections; and unique probability translations couple all intervention responses. The zero-allowed theorem then proves the finite union over exact-support subgraphs and keeps the destination stratum inside the common witness. Effective sign-condition compilers provide explicit size-dependent decision and enumeration bounds, while inference is handled separately on the compact Laplace subclass.

prose_updates.related_work: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. At the observational family containing only the empty intervention, Theorem zero-allowed-coupled-equivalence matches Dai et al.'s fixed-latent zero-allowed observational class; for a general intervention family, it extends the object to common-mechanism joint perfect interventions through an explicit finite downward-closed cover. The exact-support theorem remains the stratum-level engine and is not transferred monotonically across graph equalities. Zhou et al. study do-calculus invariances for latent directed acyclic graphs rather than cyclic parametric joint-law equality. Bongers et al. provide surgical intervention solvability semantics. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer characterize experiment designs for full second-order recovery. Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, provide the published square row-recovery comparator; the translation lift and matching-set equality are proved internally. Taeb et al. and Joint Causal Inference emphasize shared mechanisms but do not give this latent cyclic common-lift criterion. Schkoda and Drton and Wang, Kolar, and Drton motivate the separate full-law confidence-set rung rather than the population equivalence proof.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The population results are uniform for each finite labeled node set and fixed latent cardinality; their certified worst-case bounds are deliberately coarse and exponential. The proved marginal-to-joint proposition gives an exact rooted common-lift test, but the separate open-ended question still asks whether graph-generated exact-support fibers realize a smallest failure of marginal gluing. The covariance refinement witness and statistical confidence theorem remain moment-bearing submodels and do not enlarge the unrestricted population assumptions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact-support law-set equality and its finite compiler are proved on every exact nonzero-support stratum, including cancellations and lower-dimensional rank cells. The zero-allowed result is proved separately as a finite union over support subgraphs; it does not infer zero-allowed equivalence by monotonicity. Population sources are mutually independent, nonconstant, and non-Gaussian with arbitrary locations and no moment requirement. Finite second moments are used only in the stated covariance witness, and Laplace scales and inverse margins only in the statistical subclass. The theorem ranges over every finite input size but does not traverse unbounded latent cardinalities in one comparison.
